text:
Sam Carter: incident-bot says a bunch of PD pages just fired for service 'prod-inference' but the alerts look like CI job failures from the nonprod cluster. anyone seeing this?

Priya Nair: seeing it. tons of low-sev pages. N=45 in the last 3 minutes.

incident-bot: PagerDuty incident created: INC1234567 -> prod-inference (triggered by policy: ci-nonprod-failures). Escalation policy: prod-oncall-primary.

Jordan Lee: wait what — ci-nonprod-failures should be bound to nonprod-monitoring svc not prod-inference. looks like the routing binding in alerts-terraform changed.

Marta Gomez: I was just in the alerts TF workspace applying a small change to alert labels for test jobs. i did NOT intend to change service bindings. pushing the plan now to double-check.

Sam Carter: can someone temporarily silence prod-inference service? pages are drowning real alerts. @PagerDuty any way to pause escalation?

PagerDuty: Received request to add a temporary escalation pause on prod-inference. 2-step confirmation required. Reply with `CONFIRM PAUSE` to proceed.

Priya Nair: CONFIRM PAUSE

PagerDuty: Pause applied to prod-inference for 1h. Silence note: "investigating unexpected routing of nonprod alerts".

Jordan Lee: thanks. I'm opening the PD incident to track mitigation. INC1234567 assigned to oncall.

Marta Gomez: found the diff: someone changed `pagerduty_service` in alerts/overrides/nonprod.tf from "nonprod-monitor" -> "prod-inference" to test mapping. accidental commit by CI on a stale branch. pushing revert now. snippet:

```hcl
resource "pagerduty_service_attachment" "ci_nonprod" {
  service = "prod-inference" # accidental
  alert_policy = "ci-nonprod-failures"
}
```

Sam Carter: ouch. that explains it. revert + reapply should unbind. Who can run the apply?

Priya Nair: i'm on it. Running `terraform apply -target=pagerduty_service_attachment.ci_nonprod` in alerts-prod workspace. will comment when done.

incident-bot: PagerDuty INC1234567 status: acknowledged by Priya Nair.

Priya Nair: apply finished, detach plan executed, new state shows `service = "nonprod-monitor"`.

PagerDuty: Pause on prod-inference expires in 58m.

Jordan Lee: can we bulk-resolve the noisy incidents so oncall isn't blocked? we should mark the CI-driven ones as resolved.

Sam Carter: i can run PD bulk resolve on incidents matching alert key `ci-nonprod-failures` from the last 15m. executing: `pd incidents bulk-resolve --query "service:prod-inference AND alert_key:ci-nonprod-failures"`

PagerDuty: 42 incidents resolved by Sam Carter.

Marta Gomez: confirmed alerts stop firing now. looks clean. primary impact: noisy pages to prod oncall for ~7 minutes. no customer-facing errors observed.

Jordan Lee: next steps: 1) postmortem capturing root cause config drift + CI gating, 2) add a terraform plan check to block `pagerduty_service` changes without explicit owner approval, 3) add alert policy label validation in nonprod CI.

Sam Carter: also add a runbook note for temporary pause + bulk-resolve steps so oncall can act faster.

Priya Nair: creating incident follow-up doc and linking INC1234567. i'll include timeline and command history.

incident-bot: Incident INC1234567 updated: resolved.

Jordan Lee: quick retro: why did the stale branch auto-apply? is there an automation that applies plans with no manual approval in alerts-prod?

Marta Gomez: yes — we had an emergency fastpath for urgent fixes that accidentally got enabled for the alerts-prod pipeline. i'll audit and restrict it.

Sam Carter: thanks everyone. marking thread for postmortem. tagging for followups: @Priya Nair (lead), @Marta Gomez (alerts owner), @Jordan Lee (oncall/process). :thumbsup:
